title: The pool of nectar
hook: Guru Ram Das begins the pool and the town that will be named Amritsar, the pool of nectar

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jetha, from a tray of boiled grams to the fourth Guru. Your line was small beginnings.

Most towns grow up around something. A crossroads, a harbor, a mine, a railway station. Take away the thing in the middle and the town stops making sense. Today, the beginning of a city millions visit every year, one of the most famous in the world for Sikhs. It didn't grow up around a market or a fort. Before it was a city, it was a patch of land with a small natural pond, surrounded by trees. Guru Amar Das, tradition says, asked Jetha, now his son-in-law, to find a place for a new center. And Guru Ram Das began to dig.
screen: `EVERY TOWN GROWS AROUND SOMETHING.` → `A SMALL POND, AND TREES.` → `GURU RAM DAS BEGINS TO DIG.`

segments.voice: The city is Amritsar. Amrit means nectar, the water of immortality, and sar means pool: the pool of nectar. At first the settlement was called Guru ka Chak, the Guru's village, and later Ramdaspur, after Guru Ram Das. The name Amritsar came from the pool itself. Tradition says the Guru had the pond dug out and widened into a great tank, a sacred pool. Sikhs came to help, carrying earth in baskets on their heads, the same work Jetha once did at the step-well. Here's the practical genius. The Guru didn't only build a place of worship. He invited people to come and live there: traders and craftsmen of many kinds, tradition says, so the town would have its own markets and its own living. Worship and work, side by side; Kartarpur again, on a bigger scale. Sikhs tell a story about the pool, too. A young woman named Rajni, married off by her angry father to a man with leprosy, is said to have left her husband by the water while she went for food. He saw a crow dip into the pool and come out white, bathed himself, and was healed. It's a story people tell, and the tree by that spot is still honored. Guru Ram Das didn't live to see the pool finished; that would fall to his son. But he gave the town its center, and the thing in the middle was a pool of still water.
screen: `AMRIT, NECTAR. SAR, POOL.` · `SIKHS CARRIED EARTH IN BASKETS.` · `TRADERS INVITED: WORSHIP AND WORK.` · `A STORY OF HEALING AT THE WATER.` · then, large: `A TOWN AROUND A POOL.`

segments.voice: Look at still water: a glass on the table, a bowl, a puddle, a sink you've filled. Watch the surface go still, the light on it, maybe your reflection, the tiny tremble when you breathe near it. Let your mind settle the way the water does.
Amritsar. The pool of nectar; the sacred tank Guru Ram Das began, and the city that grew around it. Today's word.
Your line: a town around a pool. Before the markets came, there was still water. That's fifty-five.

howItsDone: Amritsar is the spiritual center of the Sikh world; pilgrims bathe in the sacred pool and walk around it, and many volunteer in its seva, cleaning the tank and serving in the langar.
